title: Stakeholder brief: skewed outputs and reconciliation paths
summary: Draft customer-facing update and post-incident reconciliation guide for tenants who observed skewed or inconsistent model outputs during the 2028-02-08 inference anomaly. Includes simple status-page text, recommended tenant actions, evidence package and replay options, and a decision tree for choosing recovery paths.
body:
Purpose
This is a customer-facing draft to: 1) explain in plain language what happened (skewed outputs / inconsistent responses), 2) list tenant options for verifying and reconciling affected traffic, and 3) provide a pragmatic self-serve toolkit + our support offer. Target audience: product and platform teams at impacted customers, technical leads who need replayable evidence, and CS/SEPs doing outreach.

Executive status (for status page) — short blurb
Timeline: Feb 8, 2028 — Feb 9, 2028
Impact: A subset of requests routed to a model variant experienced higher-than-expected semantic drift leading to incorrect or inconsistent outputs for approximately 0.9% of requests (most traffic unaffected). We mitigated by routing traffic away from the variant and restoring normal routing within 3 hours. No customer data was exposed or changed.
What we’re doing: We have removed the affected model variant from active routing, validated fallback health, reprocessed routing logs for affected windows, and prepared a replay/evidence package for customers to verify outputs and selectively re-run.
ETA: We are delivering tenant replay packages and runbook procedures by EOD Feb 10, 2028 (customer timezones may vary).

Plain-language timeline (detailed for customers)
- 02:07 UTC: Autoscaler placed additional capacity in eu-west region and a control-plane config pushed a compatible but unverified model variant into warm routing.
- 02:21 UTC: Internal monitoring detected increased output variance in a small shard of traffic; automatic alert created (INF-4123).
- 02:30–05:12 UTC: Variant continued serving until capacity rebalancing completed; affected window identified as 02:18–05:05 UTC (approx).
- 05:18 UTC: We initiated routing rollback to the verified baseline model and validated steady-state metrics.
- 07:00 UTC: Evidence packages prepared for customers who request replay.

What "skewed outputs" means for your product
- You may see: altered intent classification, hallucinated entities, inconsistent multi-step outputs (e.g., different facts within same session), or truncation artifacts in structured outputs.
- Most tenants will notice no user-visible change. If you saw user-facing issues we recommend following the quick checks below.

Customer quick-check (recommended immediate steps)
1) Confirm whether your tenant saw errors: run a token/sample query across a representative prompt set for the window 02:18–05:05 UTC and compare to control baseline (example queries included in evidence package).
2) If you store request/response pairs, search for anomalous responses (keywords: "N/A", repeated placeholders, sudden entity mismatches).
3) If you depend on deterministic structured outputs, run schema checks (missing fields, wrong types).
4) If you rely on embeddings, run a similarity spot-check for drift (sample 50 vectors from the period).

Decision tree for recovery (short)
- If you observed no user impact: no action required; optionally review evidence package for peace of mind.
- If you observed limited, non-customer-facing anomalies (internal logs): use tenant replay to re-evaluate and decide whether to reprocess derived artifacts.
- If you observed user-facing incorrect outputs: contact CS immediately, and follow the "rollback vs reprocess" path below.

Rollback vs reprocess (guidance)
- Rollback: If you use cached model outputs and want to avoid serving the anomalous outputs again, consider flushing caches and re-serving from a clean baseline model. This is quick and avoids user-facing repeats.
- Reprocess: If you persisted outputs into downstream storage (search indices, document store, fine-tune datasets), you should re-run the prompt set against the verified baseline and replace bad entries. Use the evidence package to identify candidates and prioritize by recency/impact.

Evidence & replay package (what we will deliver)
Each package will contain:
- Hash-indexed request/response pairs for the impacted window (truncated to protect PII and customer secrets).
- Request metadata (timestamps, routing decision id, model variant id) to help you correlate with your logs.
- A curated prompt set (20–100 queries) that reproduces common failure modes we observed.
- Suggested reprocess script (bash + example curl / SDK commands) with rate-limited replay recommendations to avoid quota spikes.
- A short integrity checklist for deciding which responses to replace.
How to request: reply to your assigned CS ticket or use the portal link included in your incident email. Expect delivery within 24 hours of request during business hours.

Self-serve replay runbook (short form)
1) Acquire package from CS or portal.
2) Run sample locally against verified_baseline model using safe params (--max-tokens 256, temperature 0.0) to compare.
3) If divergence > acceptable threshold, re-run full set at low concurrency (<= 10r/s) and re-index outputs into your downstream store.
4) Update internal audit log with verification status and ticket id.

Compensating measures we’ve implemented
- Immediate: removed problematic variant, increased routing verification checks, tightened warm-start gating for autoscales.
- Short term: added an automated semantic-drift detector for variant warmups to flag early drift at 5–10 minute windows.
- Medium term: enhance canary policy to run an internal verification prompt set before routing >0.1% traffic to a new variant.

Customer-facing FAQ (short answers)
Q: Was my data exposed?
A: No. This was a model behavior/regression; there was no unauthorized data access or mutation.

Q: Will I be charged for replays?
A: We will not bill customers for tokens consumed by our investigative replay of confirmed-affected requests. If you request additional replay services we will communicate cost impacts in advance.

Q: How long will reconciling outputs take?
A: Most customers can triage the curated package in 4–8 hours. Full reprocessing time depends on your volume and downstream indexing policies—our SEP team can assist for large pipelines.

Open questions / internal notes (for CS & SEPs)
- Need list of tenants with persisted downstream artifacts (contacts: Rajat for quick extraction).
- Confirm PII redaction level in exported request/response pairs (default: mask emails, tokens, long document bodies).
- Decide whether to offer proactive replay to top-20 impacted tenants or wait for requests.
- Draft customer-portal artifact delivery flow (Maya + Portal eng).

Next communication milestones
- Feb 9 EOD: First wave of tailored evidence packages to tenants who asked during initial outreach.
- Feb 10 EOD: General status page update moved from "investigating" to "mitigated" with links to replay how-to and support contact.
- Feb 15: Customer-facing postmortem summary (concise root cause, remediation, timeline) with final closure note.

Contact & escalation
If you are a tenant who observed user-facing anomalies, please reply to your incident contact or open a high-priority ticket with subject: "Replay request - skewed outputs - [tenant name]". For urgent technical support, email cs-urgent@redwood.ai (customers only).

Draft notes for statuspage (short):
Headline: Mitigated: limited model-variant output drift affecting small subset of requests
Body: We identified and removed a misrouted model variant that produced inconsistent outputs for a small fraction of requests between 02:18–05:05 UTC on Feb 8. Traffic has been restored to the verified baseline; we are providing replay/evidence packages for tenants to verify and reprocess if needed. No data exposure.

Internal followups (action owners)
- Rajat: export tenant list + persisted-outputs flags (due Feb 9 12:00 UTC).
- Luca: prepare replay packaging script and upload flow (due Feb 9 18:00 UTC).
- Maya: draft portal delivery UI and permission model (due Feb 10 00:00 UTC).
- Emma (owner): coordinate customer comms and finalize statuspage copy (due Feb 9 EOD).

Appendix (examples we will include in package)
- Example curl replay command (with auth examples)
- Minimal sample script to compare responses and mark replacements
- Example email template for notifying end-users if a reprocess changes previously visible outputs

End of draft

Internal TODOs: shorten statuspage headline, confirm legal signoff on wording about billing, attach final replay SLA for enterprise customers.
